issues.legal_issue: The residual limitation provision for applications applies to applications made to civil courts under laws other than the Code of Civil Procedure.
material_facts: The compensation claimant filed a petition under the Telegraph Act before a District Judge, and the electricity board argued that the petition was time-barred under Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
The claimant argued that Article 137 did not apply to petitions under the Telegraph Act.
issues.conclusion: Article 137 applies to any petition or application filed under any Act in a civil court; it is not confined to applications contemplated by or made under the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court rejected the contrary construction in Town Municipal Council, Athani v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Hubli, and applied Nityananda M. Joshi v. Life Insurance Corporation of India.
issues.legal_principle: Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, covers any other application for which no limitation period is provided elsewhere in the relevant division. Unlike Article 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908, Article 137 is not confined by ejusdem generis to applications under the Code of Civil Procedure. The Court relied on Nityananda M. Joshi v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, distinguished the Labour Court context in Town Municipal Council, Athani v. Presiding Officer, Labour Court, Hubli, and overruled Athani insofar as it confined Article 137 to applications under the Code.

predicates.civil_court_application: A person makes an application to a civil court.
predicates.application_under_another_law: The application is made under a law other than the Code of Civil Procedure.
predicates.no_other_limitation_period: No other limitation period is provided for the application in the relevant schedule.

issues.definition: When an application under another law is made to a civil court and no other limitation period is provided, the application is subject to the general limitation rule.

issues.legal_issue: A petition seeking judicial determination of compensation under the Telegraph Act before a District Judge acting as a civil court is an application governed by Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963.
material_facts: The electricity board cut and removed trees from the claimant’s property to lay electric lines and assessed compensation.
The claimant disputed the sufficiency of the compensation and filed a petition before the District Judge seeking enhanced compensation under the Telegraph Act.
The board contended that the petition was filed more than three years after notice of the compensation assessment; the District Judge held it time-barred, and the High Court set that decision aside.
The petition was made to the District Judge for judicial determination, and the Telegraph Act provided for court processes and payment into court in relevant disputes.
issues.conclusion: The District Judge acted as a civil court in dealing with the petition, so the petition was an application within Article 137. The Court allowed the appeal and set aside the High Court’s judgment, thereby restoring the District Judge’s time-bar ruling.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 10 and 16 of the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, a dispute over the sufficiency of compensation is referred to the District Judge for determination. Sections 16(4) and 34 support the conclusion that the District Judge acts as a court, and section 3(15) of the General Clauses Act identifies the District Judge as the judge of the principal civil court of original jurisdiction unless the context indicates otherwise. Where a statute refers a matter to a court of record without further provision, the court determines it as a court: National Telephone Co. Ltd. v. The Postmaster-General. The petition therefore falls within Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963; Kerala State Electricity Board v. Paravathi Amma was referred to.

predicates.compensation_dispute_proceeding: A person seeks a judicial decision on a dispute about compensation for property damage caused in the exercise of statutory powers.
predicates.district_judge_decides_as_civil_court: The matter is referred to a District Judge who acts as a civil court in deciding it.
predicates.judicial_determination_required: The governing legal scheme provides for the dispute to be determined judicially by the District Judge.

issues.definition: When a compensation dispute is referred for judicial determination to a District Judge acting as a civil court, the application is subject to the general limitation rule.
